profile.address: near NE 30th Avenue and NE Evergreen Road, Hillsboro, OR
profile.reading: Aligned DC - PDX-01 sits on a 27-acre campus near NE 30th Avenue and NE Evergreen Road in Hillsboro, Oregon, Aligned first facility in the Pacific Northwest market. Per the operator own January 2023 press release announcing the expansion, the initial building on this campus, PDX-01, was designed for 72 megawatts of critical capacity, with a second, planned building targeted for an additional 36 megawatts, bringing the eventual campus total to roughly 108 megawatts against 120 megawatts of utility capacity secured for the site. The release described the Hillsboro location as chosen to support hyperscale and large-enterprise demand in the Pacific Northwest. The campus sits within an Oregon Enterprise Zone, a state and local program that provides property tax abatement for qualifying industrial and data-center investment, consistent with abatement programs used by other operators in the Hillsboro market. Aligned, formerly known as Aligned Energy, describes its overall footprint today as more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of contracted and available capacity across the Americas, with Latin American operations run under the ODATA brand. Ownership has shifted substantially over the company history, most recently with an October 2025 agreement for a consortium called AI Infrastructure Partnership, combining BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX, to acquire all of Aligned equity from majority owner Macquarie Asset Management and its co-investors in a deal valued near 40 billion dollars, with a close indicated around July 2026 in Aligned own materials though not independently confirmed by a dedicated press release this session. No specific tenant is named for PDX-01 in any source reviewed. Aligned own facility naming pattern, PDX for the Portland airport code plus a sequence number, mirrors the airport-code shorthand the company also uses for its IAD, ORD, and DFW markets, a convention common across the colocation industry.
profile.research_note: 72 MW for the initial building (PDX-01), 108 MW eventual two-building campus total, and 120 MW utility capacity sourced to Aligned own Jan 2023 PR. Oregon Enterprise Zone status noted as a program type consistent with other Hillsboro operators, not independently verified for this specific parcel this session.

profile.reading: Aligned Data Centers DFW-04 sits on a 44-acre campus at 601 North Star Road in Plano, Texas, a separate site from Aligned original 19-acre DFW-01 and DFW-02 campus elsewhere in Plano. Aligned own Dallas location page confirms the address and acreage for this fourth Dallas-Fort Worth building, but no dedicated press release describing DFW-04 specific capacity in megawatts, its square footage, or its construction or opening status could be located this session. That gap is noted honestly here rather than filled with a figure carried over from the DFW-02 or DFW-03 buildings elsewhere in the Dallas-Fort Worth market, since Aligned facilities vary considerably in size even within the same metro area, and DFW-04 sits on a notably larger acreage than the original campus. Aligned, formerly known as Aligned Energy, describes its overall footprint today as more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of contracted and available capacity across the Americas, with Latin American operations run under the ODATA brand. Ownership has shifted substantially over the company history: Macquarie Infrastructure Partners first invested in April 2018 alongside BlueMountain Capital Management, Mubadala Investment Company took a minority stake in August 2023 with Macquarie Asset Management confirmed as majority partner, CenterSquare Investment Management invested in April 2024, and Macquarie led a capital raise exceeding 12 billion dollars in January 2025. In October 2025 a consortium called AI Infrastructure Partnership, combining BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX, agreed to acquire all of Aligned equity from Macquarie and its co-investors in a deal valued near 40 billion dollars, with a close indicated around July 2026 in Aligned own materials though not independently confirmed by a dedicated press release this session.

reading:
Aligned Data Centers is the full legal name of the company this registry also carries under the shorter form Aligned, where the fuller corporate profile sits. Both rows describe one Dallas, Texas headquartered wholesale and colocation developer, previously held by Macquarie Asset Management and the subject of an approximately 40 billion dollar acquisition by the AI Infrastructure Partnership, MGX and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners announced in October 2025. Closing of that transaction is not confirmed in this entry. The duplicate row is kept rather than deleted so that the facilities attached to each spelling of the name stay traceable.

What this row actually holds is two buildings. The first is PDX-01 in Hillsboro, Oregon, which Aligned publishes as a 27 acre campus at the corner of Northeast 30th Avenue and Northeast Evergreen Road, Hillsboro 97124, designed to Tier III standards. The second is DFW-04 in Plano, Texas, which Aligned publishes as a 44 acre campus and addresses as 601 North Star Road, Plano 75074. The mapped building the registry stores, and the coordinate attached to it, sit at 401 North Star Road. Both numbers are on the same road and describe the same campus, so this reads as a difference between the operator's own page and the county address point rather than two different sites, but neither number should be presented here as settled.

Aligned's Dallas page lists three further campuses that do not appear under this row at all, DFW-01 and DFW-02 sharing 2800 Summit Avenue in Plano on 19 acre sites, and DFW-03 at 3801 Britton Road in Mansfield on a 27 acre site.

What is not published is the power. For neither PDX-01 nor DFW-04 does Aligned state an IT load, a utility service size, a standby diesel generator count or any on-site generation. Acreage and a design tier are the only quantities the operator puts in public for these two buildings, and no city or county document found here supplies the missing numbers. Aligned does publish a megawatt figure elsewhere, describing a 540 MW next generation campus in northwest Texas that it calls Project Caprock, but it does not say whether that figure is critical IT load or the utility service the campus expects to draw, and Caprock is not one of the sites recorded under this row.
